units.function: Tool action canonicalization/hash/HMAC envelope plus sensitive-content summarization and heuristic prompt-injection validation for Tool arguments/results.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on Node cryptography and shared server redaction helpers; Tool Access/Gateway execution and approval paths consume signatures, decoded arguments, summaries and validation errors. It is a security utility but remains server-specific through environment-secret resolution.
units.keyDataModels: Canonical Tool arguments, versioned HS256 signed envelope bound to Invocation ID/tool name/optional approval snapshot/execute-on-approve flag, dedicated signing secret, redacted summary/hash/findings and content-validation error reason code.
units.lifecycle: Arguments are recursively key-sorted and serialized, optionally signed with a dedicated HMAC key, decoded and timing-safe verified against expected context before JSON parsing into arguments. Content validation summarizes/redacts sensitive values, scans four prompt-injection regex classes and either returns findings/value/summary or throws according to modes.
units.testAssessment: The previously audited 82-line suite proves tamper detection, Invocation/tool binding, dedicated-key requirement, basic redaction and one prompt-injection block. Implementation review finds untested semantic and robustness gaps: sensitiveMode=redact only transforms plain objects; strings and arrays are returned unchanged even when the summary detects/redacts a Secret. promptInjectionMode=redact records findings but does not redact or quarantine the content. Signed blobs and nested payloads are decoded/parsed before verification with no byte/depth limit. Canonicalization has no explicit handling for undefined, bigint, cyclic/non-JSON values, Unicode normalization or numeric edge cases. HMAC envelope lacks key ID/rotation, issued/expiry time, nonce/replay scope, Company/Work/Agent/Connector/action/policy/data binding and result signature. Shared symmetric instance key gives no execution-node identity. Heuristic regex scanning is bypassable and false-positive prone.
units.designRationale: Bind reviewed Tool parameters to one Invocation/tool using a dedicated secret, prevent ordinary authentication secrets from becoming signing keys, and stop obvious Secret/prompt-injection content from silently entering Agent context.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical ActionEnvelope and ResultEnvelope that preserve exact human-approved bytes and enforce the data egress/ingress firewall at a Connector execution node.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the versioned envelope, deterministic canonicalization, domain-separated context binding, dedicated key and timing-safe verification. Use a standard canonical JSON/CBOR profile with strict input limits; bind Company/Work/ResponsibilityContract/Agent/Connector/tool+schema version/action digest/permissions/data contract/approval/policy version/nonce/iat/exp; support key IDs and rotation or node public-key signatures; verify before expensive decode where possible; sign Result/Evidence. Replace misleading redact modes with actual recursive transformation or explicit quarantine/block and layered content-security classifiers.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signed object may include an approval snapshot but does not require or semantically validate accountable human, approval decision, responsibility/data contract or execution expiry. A shared service HMAC proves only key possession, not which Connector node executed the action. Redact modes can return the original sensitive or adversarial bytes, breaking the evidence/data-boundary promise.
